subject: Renewal coordination — capacity ceiling & committed slab for 32 GPUs
messages:
From: Mira Shah <mira@cleardata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cleardata.com
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32)

Hi Hannah,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for the Dedicated pool is coming up in mid-April and we want to explore doubling our committed capacity from 16 to 32 GPUs. Usage has spiked in Q1 and our latency-sensitive workloads need predictable throughput.

Key asks: 
- Target go-live for the expanded pool: 2027-05-01 (we can be flexible a couple weeks)
- Revised per-GPU reserved hourly pricing for the 32-GPU slab, with 12- and 24-month term options
- A throughput SLO or minimum tokens/sec per GPU guidance for our mix (inference + streaming chat)
- Any ramp credits or onboarding credits for the first 30 days as we shift traffic and validate canaries

I’ve attached our current usage report for Q1 and a short note from infra about rollout constraints. Procurement (cc’d) will lead contract/legal once we have a commercial position.

Thanks — can we get a pricing proposal this week?

Best,
Mira
Customer Success Manager
ClearData Systems
Attachment: current_usage_report_q1.pdf (report stub)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mira Shah <mira@cleardata.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@cleardata.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32)

Mira — thanks for the detail and the usage report. We can absolutely support a 32-GPU committed pool for your account. A few quick clarifying questions before Dev and I put together a formal amendment:

- Do you expect steady-state 32 GPUs in production, or should we stage a 16→32 ramp over 30 days?
- Any hard latency SLOs (p95/p99) we should account for in the throughput analysis?
- Are there regulatory constraints (data residency/region) we need on the Dedicated cluster?

High-level timeline: if we lock terms by Apr 15 we can schedule capacity to meet your 2027-05-01 target. Dev, can you draft the per-hour reserved pricing options (12/24m) and a recommended throughput guarantee for their workload?

I’ll coordinate a 30-min call with Mira and procurement for Thursday to run through the amendments.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Mira Shah <mira@cleardata.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@cleardata.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32) — proposed commercial + SLAs

Hi Mira / Hannah,

Based on the Q1 usage profile and the mix of short-chat sessions + batched inference in the report, here is a practical commercial proposal we can put into an amendment: 

Summary (all numbers USD):
- Current baseline (16 GPUs) reserved rate: $2.40 / GPU-hour (12m term)
- Proposed 32-GPU slab (12-month term): $2.05 / GPU-hour reserved (effective ~14.6% discount vs current 16-GPU rate)
- Proposed 32-GPU slab (24-month term): $1.85 / GPU-hour reserved (effective ~22.9% discount)
- Activation fee: one-time $0 for committed capacity increases (we can waive the onboarding fee)

Throughput / SLO proposal (engineering-backed):
- Baseline throughput guarantee: 2.4k tokens/sec aggregate per GPU for your QPS distribution (with 95% of requests under 1s latency under normal load)
- Isolation: Dedicated pool reserved to your tenant, autoscaling knob disabled for the reserved slab (we can add burst buffer for short spikes)
- Canary: we recommend a 7–14 day canary at 50% traffic to validate tail latency; Redwood will provide traffic shaping and KV-prefix cache recommendations

Ramp credits / operational support:
- Ramp credit: 10% credit applied to first 30 days of billing for the newly committed GPUs (applies to reserved portion only)
- Dedicated onboarding: one free technical design review (2 hours) + one onsite/remote readiness call

Open items for legal/commercial:
- Term start date and commitment baseline (do we bill the full 32 from day one or bill 16 + incremental as capacity is activated?) — our standard approach is bill full slab from activation date.
- SLAs: we can commit to the throughput guidance above; for monetary SLA we propose an availability SLA for the reserved pool (99.5% monthly uptime) with service credits as outlined in the amendment.

I’ve attached a draft amendment and a short throughput model. If you want I can also include a simple amortized cost table showing effective hourly per-GPU cost given your average monthly utilization.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Amendment_v3.pdf, throughput_analysis.xlsx

—
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Bell <ethan.bell@cleardata.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Mira Shah <mira@cleardata.com>, procurement@cleardata.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32) — proposed commercial + SLAs

Dev / Hannah,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed proposal. A few follow-ups from procurement / infra after an internal review: 

1) Pricing: the 24-month price looks reasonable but procurement is asking for a further 3% reduction on the 24-month per-hour rate if we commit to a firm auto-renew clause. Can Redwood confirm?

2) Billing cadence: we prefer billing to start on a staged activation basis (bill the incremental GPUs once they are live) — this helps our internal chargeback and cash flow. Would Redwood accept staged billing instead of charging the full slab from activation?

3) Ramp credit: can you extend the ramp credit to cover the first 45 days for the incremental 16 GPUs only? That eases our migration risk.

4) Data residency: some workloads must remain in us-west region; please confirm the dedicated pool will be provisioned in us-west and that backups for logs stay in region.

5) Compliance artifacts: procurement needs SOC2 Type II evidence and a recent penetration test report before final sign-off.

If we can get the 3% concession and staged billing cadence + extended ramp credit, we can move to legal and aim to sign within 10 business days. Happy to take a 30-min call with Hannah to finalize.

Regards,
Ethan Bell
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClearData Systems
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Bell <ethan.bell@cleardata.com>, Mira Shah <mira@cleardata.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@cleardata.com
Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + request to double reserved GPUs (16→32) — next steps

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses while we prepare the redlines: 

- Pricing concession: yes, we can extend an additional 3% on the 24-month committed per-hour rate in exchange for an auto-renew clause; commercial will draft language.
- Billing cadence: we can support staged billing for the incremental 16 GPUs (bill incremental as they’re activated) — we’ll capture this in the amendment and the activation schedule.
- Ramp credit: we can extend the ramp credit to 45 days for the incremental GPUs only.
- Region: confirmed — the dedicated pool will be provisioned in us-west with log retention options scoped to region; Marcus will attach the region configuration notes for the infra team.
- Compliance: Hannah to share SOC2 Type II and penetration test summary via the secure compliance portal; legal will include standard certification clauses.

Next step: I’ll schedule a short alignment call for Tue 2027-03-30 09:00 PT to run through the amendment draft and DocuSign flow. Dev/Marcus will bring the amendment + throughput appendix. If legal/procurement want early access to the DocuSign draft, I’ll send the link by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
